The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[22] ﴿You were heedless of this, so We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp.﴾

﴿You were heedless of this, so We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp.﴾ Concerning the one addressed by this, there are three opinions:

The first: that he is the Prophet (ﷺ). The verse came as a parenthetical sentence within the account of the Hereafter, to point out the favor of being informed of this and being made aware of it, and then the intensity of the penetration of sight regarding it and the grasping of its obscure aspects after the mind had been entirely empty of it. The meaning: "You were heedless of this Qur'an before it was revealed to you, so We removed your covering by sending it down to you; so your sight today is sharp, penetrating and strong: you see what they do not see, and you know what they do not know." Similar to it is the verse ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was﴾ [al-Shura: 52].

The second: that he is the disbeliever, and that the speech is on the assumption of a saying, i.e., it is said to him: "You were heedless of this which you now witness of the terrors, so We removed your covering by making it clear to you and showing it to your eyes, until you saw it and witnessed it, and heedlessness departed from you." Similar to it, concerning the disbelievers, is the verse ﴿How well they will hear and see on the day they come to Us﴾ [Maryam: 38], and the verse ﴿If only you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and heard"﴾ [as-Sajdah: 12].

The third: that he is the human being in general, based on His words ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾ [Qaf: 21]. The intended meaning is that the covering was removed from the righteous and the wicked alike, and each saw what he was heading toward.

Ibn Jarir relied upon the third opinion as the most preferable.

al-Zamakhshari said: Heedlessness is treated as if it were a covering with which his whole body was covered, or a veil with which his eyes were covered, so that he sees nothing. When the Day of Resurrection comes, he awakens, heedlessness and its covering depart from him, and he sees what he did not see of the truth.

al-Qashani said in interpreting the verse: "You were heedless of this" because of your being veiled by the senses and sensible things and your distraction from it, due to your occupation with the outward over the inward. "So We removed from you, through death, your material, bodily covering with which you were veiled." ﴿So your sight today is sharp﴾, i.e., your perception of what you were heedless of and did not believe in its existence, strong, as you witness it. End of quotation.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:

[23] ﴿And his companion will say, "This is what is ready with me."﴾

﴿And his companion will say﴾: that is, the companion of this human being who is brought on the Day of Resurrection, accompanied by a driver and a witness. This companion is either the angel (malak) assigned to him in the world to record his deeds, who is the watcher who goes before him, or the devil (shaytan) who is appointed to him as an associate to lead him astray. The latter is the more apparent, as al-Zamakhshari adopted, based on the verse: ﴿We shall appoint for him a devil, and he will be his companion﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 36]. Supporting this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿His companion will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress"﴾ [Qaf: 27]. ﴿This is what is ready with me﴾: that is, this is a thing present with me, prepared and guarded.

The pointing (of "this") refers, according to the first view, to what is in his record of deeds, and according to the second, to the person himself. That is: "This is what is ready with me for Hell, which I prepared for it by my misleading him."

Al-Qashani said:

﴿And his companion will say﴾: that is, from the devil of illusion (wahm), who deceived him with outward appearances and veiled him from inner realities: "This is what is ready with me," prepared for Hell. That is, the subjugation of illusion over him became apparent in his turning toward the lower direction, and in its gaining mastery over him and enslaving him in the pursuit of bodily pleasures, until it prepared him for Hell at the bottom of nature (p-٥٥٠٤). End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 50, verse 24:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿Cast, both of you, into Hell every stubborn disbeliever.﴾

﴿Cast, both of you, into Hell every stubborn disbeliever.﴾ This is an address from God, exalted is He, to the driver and the witness, on the basis that they are two angels, not one angel combining both descriptions; or to two of the keepers of the Fire; or to one. The dual form of the agent is treated as the dual of the verb, and its repetition is on the basis that its origin is: "Cast! Cast!" Then the second verb was deleted and its pronoun was kept with the first verb, so the pronoun was made dual to indicate what has been mentioned. Or the alif is a substitute for the nun of emphasis, because it is changed into an alif in pause, so the continuous speech was made to follow that. These are aspects that they have mentioned.

Ibn Jarir said: The command was given to the companion, and it is in a single form, in the manner of addressing two people. In this there are two aspects of interpretation:

The first: that the companion is in the sense of two, like "al-rasul" (the messenger), and the noun that takes the form of the singular for the singular, the dual and the plural. So he returned His saying, "Cast (dual)," to the meaning.

The second: that it is as some of the scholars of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'arabiyyah) used to say, namely: the Arabs address one person or a group with what they address two people with. So they say to a man: "Woe to you! Drive them (dual) on, and urge them (dual) on," as one said:

"So I said to my two companions: Do not hold us back, by uprooting its roots, and let him chew the wormwood."

And Abu Tharwan said:

"If you two (dual) deter me, O son of 'Affan, I shall be deterred, * and if you two leave me, I shall defend an honour that is protected."

(p-5505) The reason for this among them is that the least number of a man's helpers with his camels and sheep is two, and likewise the least number of a travelling company is three; so the speech of the one was applied to his two companions. Do you not see that poets most often say: "O my two companions, O my two friends"? End of quotation.

And "al-kaffar" (the one who is extreme in denying the Oneness of God, exalted is He, and what His Messenger brought, may the prayers of God be upon him) is the one who exaggerates in denial.

And "al-'anid" is the one who is obstinate against the truth and the path of guidance, not listening to any proof in the face of his disbelief, and he has gone beyond obstinacy with a description:

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[25] ﴿Forbidder of good, transgressor, doubter﴾

﴿Forbidder of good﴾: that is, of all good, which is Islam, or wealth. Ibn Jarir favored that here it means every right that is due to God or to a human being in one's wealth, because nothing is specified from it; thus it indicates that it is every good whose withholding from the one who seeks it is possible. ﴿Transgressor﴾: that is, exceeding the limit in aggression against people by abuse and obscenity in speech, and with his hand by domineering and violent oppression, unjustly. As Qatadah said: "transgressor in his speech, his conduct and his affairs."

﴿Doubter﴾: that is, one who doubts the truth, or one who casts his companion into doubt despite the abundance of proofs.

Al-Qashani said: The address in ﴿Cast﴾ [Qaf: 24] is to the driver and the witness, who ruin him, throw him down and destroy him into the lowest depths of the abyss of corporeal matter, and the pit of the well of the dark nature, into the fires of deprivation. Or it is addressed to Malik. The purpose of the doubling of the agent is the repetition of the act, as if he said: "Cast, cast," because of his dominance over them in driving away and casting down toward the lower direction. The first view is strengthened by the fact that He enumerated the destructive vices which made them deserve the punishment of Hell and their falling into the fires of the Blazing Hell, and He made clear that they belong to the category of knowledge and action. Both ingratitude and withholding good stem from the excess of the bestial, appetitive power, due to its immersion in its pleasures and its use of God Exalted's blessings in other than their proper places, through sins, and veiling itself from the Benefactor who bestowed them; and it is among its rights to remind one of Him and to stir one to thank Him, and its relentless pursuit of them because of its excessive eagerness for them, so it withholds them from those deserving them. He mentioned both in the form of intensification, to indicate the firm rootedness of the two vices in him and their dominance over him, and his deep immersion in them, which necessitates falling from the rank of natural disposition into the bottom of the well of nature. Both vacillation and transgression stem from the excess of the irascible power, its dominance due to excessive satanic nature, and departure from the limit of justice. All four belong to the category of corruption of action. Doubt and associating partners both stem from deficiency of the rational power, and its fall from natural disposition by neglecting it regarding God, and its deviation from the limit of the intellectual power; and that belongs to the category of corruption of knowledge. End of quotation.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26] ﴿Who set up another god along with Allah, so cast him into the severe punishment.﴾

﴿Who set up another god along with Allah﴾ means: who worshipped alongside Him another object of worship from among His creation. ﴿So cast him into the severe punishment﴾ means: the punishment of Hell.

A subtle point:

The relative pronoun (al-mawsul) is either a subject (mubtada') containing the meaning of a conditional (shart), whose predicate is ﴿so cast him﴾; or an object (maf'ul) of a hidden verb that is explained by ﴿so cast him﴾; or an apposition (badal) of ﴿every disbeliever﴾ [Qaf: 24], in which case ﴿so cast him﴾ is a repetition for emphasis. It has been said regarding the last view that it contradicts what the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) have mentioned, namely that between the emphasized and the emphasizing element there must be such close connection as prevents coordination (al-'atf). It has been answered: this is of the type of "your right, then your right" (wa haqquka thumma haqquka), where the difference between the emphasized and the emphasizing, or between the explained and the explaining, is treated as the difference between two distinct entities in a rhetorical sense. And if "the severe punishment" were taken to be a kind of the punishment of Hell and one of its terrors, on the basis of the type of "His angels, His messengers, and Jibril" [al-Baqarah: 98], it would be good.

Al-Shihab (after quoting the above) said: Ibn Malik said in (al-Tashil): separating the two clauses in emphasis with "thumma" (then), provided there is no ambiguity, is better than joining them; and some grammarians mentioned the fa' (then/so). The Zamakhshari mentioned the waw (and) too in (al-Jathiyah), and the grammarians agree that it is a terminological emphasis (ta'kid istilahi), and the statement of the scholars of meanings in absolutely prohibiting it is not sound. End of quotation.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[27] ﴿His companion will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he was in far error."﴾

﴿His companion will say﴾, i.e., the companion of this disbelieving human being who withholds good, and he is his devil (shaytan) who was assigned to him in the world, disowning him. ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress﴾, i.e., by misleading him, preventing him from Islam, and making another god along with You. ﴿But he was in far error﴾, i.e., on a path deviating from the way of guidance, in a far deviation by his own doing.

Al-Qashani said: The saying of the devil, ﴿I did not make him transgress﴾, etc., is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves﴾ [Ibrahim: 22], because if he had not been in error away from the path of tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness), far from the original innate nature (fitrah) by turning toward the lower direction and being covered by the natural dark veils, he would not have accepted the whisperings of the devil, and he would have accepted the inspiration of the angel. So the sin is only upon him through veiling himself from the light of the fitrah and acquiring kinship with the devil in darkness. End of quote.

Ibn Jarir said: Allah, exalted is He, informed about the saying of the disbeliever's companion to him on the Day of Resurrection, as a notice to His servants that some of them will disown others on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿He will say, "Do not dispute before Me, for I had already presented to you the warning."﴾

﴿He will say, "Do not dispute before Me, for I had already presented to you the warning."﴾ That is: Do not dispute today in the abode of recompense and the station of reckoning; there is no benefit in your disputing, for I had already presented to you in the world the warning for whoever disbelieved in Me, disobeyed Me, and opposed My command and My prohibition, in My Books and through the tongues of My messengers.

Al-Qashani said: The prohibition against disputing does not mean its cessation, but rather the lack of its benefit and the non-hearing of it. It is as if it were said: "No dispute will be heard by Me. The presentation of the warning has been established and confirmed, when it was possible for you to benefit from it, since your faculties were sound and your capacity remained intact. But you did not benefit from it, and you paid it no heed at all, until the dark dispositions became firmly rooted in your souls, veiled your hearts, the veil was realized, and the word of punishment became binding." End of quotation.

And from Ibn ʿAbbas: They offered excuses without a valid excuse, so Allah nullified their argument and rejected their statement.

The Interpretation of His Words:

[29] ﴿The word is not changed before Me, and I am not unjust to the servants.﴾

﴿The word is not changed before Me.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: It is not altered, the word I spoke to you in this world, which is His saying: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together﴾ [Hud: 119], nor My decree which I decreed concerning them therein.

﴿And I am not unjust to the servants.﴾ That is: I do not punish anyone for another's sin, but for his own sin after the proof has been established against him.

Al-Qashani said: ﴿And I am not unjust﴾ in that I bestowed the capacity (isti'dad), and I made manifest the perfection suited to it, and I guided you to the path of acquiring it. Rather, it is you who wrong yourselves by acquiring what contradicts it, and by squandering the capacity through placing light in darkness, and exchanging what perishes for what endures.

Notes (tanbihat):

First: The apparent meaning of the verses is that this mutual speech is literal, since there is no barrier to it. Some exegetes held that it is figurative (majaz).

Al-Qashani said: All these exchanges are spiritual (ma'nawiyyah), represented in the manner of imagery and depiction, to firm up the meaning in the heart when its likeness is imprinted in the imagination. The disbeliever's claim that the devil made him transgress, and the devil's denial of it, is an expression of the conflict and tug-of-war occurring between his two powers: the imaginative (wahmiyyah) and the rational ('aqliyyah); indeed, between every two opposing powers within him, such as the irascible (ghadabiyyah) and the appetitive (shahwiyyah), for example. That is why He said: ﴿Do not dispute before Me﴾ [Qaf: 28]. Since the two matters in his existence are the rational and the imaginative, the root of the dispute is between them. Likewise, dispute occurs between every two interlocutors debating a matter, expecting benefit or pleasure. They cease while their goal is attained, but when it is denied them, they bring upon themselves loss and punishment through their striving. They dispute with each other, or each attributes the cause of that to the other, due to their veiling from tawhid, and each disowns his sin out of love of himself. For this reason, Haritha, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "I saw the people of the Fire quarrelling with one another," and he (ﷺ) approved his words. End quote.

Second: If you ask: why was the waw dropped from the phrase ﴿Said his companion﴾ [Qaf: 27] and mentioned in the first? I say: because it was taken as a fresh sentence, as sentences in the narration of speech are resumed, as you have seen in the narration of the exchange between Musa and Fir'awn.

If you say: where is the exchange? I say: when his companion said: ﴿This is what I have ready﴾ [Qaf: 23], followed by his words: ﴿Said his companion: Our Lord, I did not make him transgress﴾ [Qaf: 27], and then: ﴿Do not dispute﴾ [Qaf: 28], it is known that there was an exchange from the disbeliever, but it was omitted, being indicated by the context. It is as if, when the companion said: ﴿This is what I have ready﴾, the disbeliever said: "My Lord, he made me transgress," and when the disbeliever said that, the companion said: "I did not make him transgress." When He related the words of the companion and the disbeliever, it was as if someone said: "Then what did Allah, Exalted is He, say?" So it was said: ﴿He said: Do not dispute before Me﴾ [Qaf: 28]. The waw was mentioned in the first sentence (p-٥٥١٠) because it is the beginning of the exchange, and it must be conjoined to show the combination of its meaning and the meaning of what precedes it in occurrence, namely the coming of every soul with the two angels, and the saying of its companion what he said to it. This is the summary of what is in al-Kashshaf.

Third: It was permitted that His saying ﴿with the warning﴾ [Qaf: 28] be such that the bā' is extra in the object; or that it is a circumstantial clause (hal) of the subject or object, the bā' being for accompaniment (mulabasah) or association (ma'iyyah). The meaning: I have sent forward this word as a warning to you with it; or while the word is accompanied by the warning; or it is from ﴿do not dispute﴾ with the interpretation of the warning being presented with knowledge of it, i.e., do not dispute knowing it. This is so that the circumstantial clause is valid, and there is concomitance between it and its governing element according to their terminology.

Fourth: His saying ﴿The word is not changed before Me﴾ indicates that there is no failing in Allah's threat, just as there is no breaking of Allah's promise. This refutes the Murji'ah (a sect holding that faith is not affected by sin), who said: what came in the Qur'an of threat is intimidation, and Allah does not actualize any of it. They said: the generous, when he promises, fulfills and complies; when he threatens, he breaks and pardons. Related by al-Razi.

The line of argument: if what they said were correct, it would entail the alteration of His word and failing in His report, exalted is He above that, while the nature of sin requires punishment, unless the sinner repents from it, or Allah, Exalted is He, wills to pardon it.

Fifth: They mentioned several aspects regarding the secret of the intensive form in ﴿zallam﴾ (one who wrongs greatly):

Among them: that the form (fa''al) has come in the sense of (fa'il), so this is from that.

Among them: considering the multitude of creation.

Among them: that what is ascribed, customarily, to kings of injustice under their oppression is, if great, great, and if small, small. So Allah's dominion over everything He owns, sanctified is His essence above what the forsaken imagine, and we seek refuge in Allah, is that injustice is ascribed to Him under the comprehensiveness of every existent.

(p-٥٥١١)

**The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:**

[30] ﴿On the Day We will say to Hell, "Are you full?" and it will say, "Is there any more?"﴾

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Regarding this, the people of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) hold two views.

The first: its meaning is "there is no more." From Mujahid, who said: Allah promised it, "I will surely fill you," so He said, "Shall I not have fulfilled you?" It said, "Is there any way to more?!"

The second: its meaning is "Add more for me."

That is, the interrogative is a rebuke (*inkari*) according to the first view, meaning negation, and this is supported by the verse ﴿I will surely fill Hell with the jinn and mankind all together﴾ [Hud: 119], and the Qur'an explains one part of itself by another. According to the second view, the interrogative is affirmative (*taqriri*), indicating its vastness, such that whoever enters it will enter, and there is still space and emptiness in it, as if it is seeking more.

If it is said: The second view, that there is emptiness in it, contradicts the explicit wording in His saying ﴿I will surely fill Hell﴾ [Hud: 119], and so on. I say: There is no contradiction between them as is imagined, because "filling" may mean that no tier of it is empty of those who dwell in it, even if there is a large space within it, just as it is said: "The town is full of its people; there is no empty house in it," despite the buildings and courtyards between them. Or this is in consideration of two states: the emptiness is at the time when its people first enter it, then the devils and their like are driven into it, and it becomes full.

**A note:**

A group of scholars held that the speech in the verse is figurative (*majaz*), in the manner of allegorical metaphor (*isti'ara tamthiliyya*), and that Hell, because of its intense blazing and roaring and the falling of the disbelievers and sinners and their being hurled into it, is as if it were seeking more. Others held that this is literal (*haqiqa*).

Al-Nasir, in *al-Intisaf*, said: We believe that Hell's questioning and its answer are literal, and that Allah Most High creates in it the perception for that, under its condition. How could we posit otherwise, when reports have come and are mutually reinforcing on this? Among them is this verse, and among them is the hadith: "The contention (*lijaj*) of Paradise and the Fire," and among them is: "Its complaint to its Lord, so He permitted it two breaths." Even if these are not explicit texts, they are apparent meanings (*zawahir*) that must be taken in their literal realities, because we are obliged to believe the apparent meaning unless an obstacle prevents it, and there is no obstacle here, for power is capable and reason permits it, and the apparent meanings require the occurrence of what reason permits. Something like this has definitively occurred in this world, such as "the greeting of trees and the glorification of pebbles in the palm of the Prophet (ﷺ) and in the hands of his companions." If the door of figurative usage and deviation from the apparent meaning were opened in the details of such statements, the breach would widen and many people would stray from the truth. This is not like the apparent meanings in theological matters (*ilahiyyat*) whose apparent sense reason does not permit believing, for deviation from the apparent wording there is necessary in submission to the proofs of reason that guide to the correct belief. End.

Al-Shihab (al-Khafaji) said: This is a fine statement, and matters of the Hereafter should not be measured by matters of this world. End.

And do not forget what we have said many times: that language is not confined to literal usage, and that most of language is figurative, not literal, as al-Suyuti explained in *al-Muzhir* and al-Jurjani in *Asrar al-Balagha*. The many Arabic examples support figurative usage, and there is no objection to it, apart from it being more eloquent, as they have established. In sum, the noble wording admits both, and Allah knows best.

"Yawma" (on the Day) is in the accusative, governed by *zallam* (the Oppressor) or by an implied verb, such as: "remember" and "warn." And *al-mazid* is either a verbal noun (*masdar*) like *al-majid*, or a passive participle (*ism maf'ul*) like *al-mabi'*.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 50, verse 31:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[31] ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing, not far away.﴾

﴿And Paradise will be brought near﴾, i.e., it will be made close, or drawn near. ﴿To the God-fearing﴾, i.e., to those who feared their Lord, so they feared His punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿Not far away﴾, i.e., a place not far away. So it is an adjective of the adverb of place which has taken its place, or a circumstantial qualifier of "Paradise." Its being masculine is because it is an adjective of a masculine noun, i.e., "a thing not far away," or because "Paradise" is interpreted as "garden," or because it follows the pattern of a verbal noun (maṣdar), which in its nature applies to both masculine and feminine, so it is treated accordingly and given its ruling. In any case, it serves as emphasis and to prevent a metaphorical reading, so that after mentioning that it has been brought near, one does not say: it needs no further description as "not far away."

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[32] ﴿This is what you were promised, for every oft-returning, watchful one﴾

﴿This﴾ means: the reward, or the drawing near (to Paradise). ﴿What you were promised﴾, O God-fearing ones. ﴿For every oft-returning﴾, i.e., one who turns back from disobedience to God to obedience to Him, repenting of his sins. ﴿Watchful﴾, i.e., one who guards the obligations of God and what He has entrusted to him.

Al-Qashani said: i.e., one who keeps watch over the purity of his natural disposition (fitrah) and his original light, lest it be clouded by the darkness of the self. And "li-kull" (for every) is a substitute (badal) for "lil-muttaqin" (for the God-fearing), with the preposition repeated.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 50, verse 33:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[33] ﴿Whoever feared the Most Merciful unseen and came with a penitent heart.﴾

﴿Whoever feared the Most Merciful unseen﴾ means: he feared Allah in his secret self. Al-Qashani said: that is, whoever has attained the quality of fear (khashyah), such that fear has become his station (maqam). The word "man" (whoever) is a substitute of a substitute (badal ba'd badal), or a predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: they are those who feared. Or it is a subject whose predicate is what follows it, with the interpretation: it will be said to them, "Enter it..." etc.

﴿And came with a penitent heart﴾ means: he came to his Lord with a heart that repents of its sins, returning from what He dislikes to what pleases Him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 50, verses 34–35:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[34–35] ﴿Enter it in peace. That is the Day of Eternity.﴾ ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, and with Us is more.﴾ [Qaf: 35]

﴿Enter it in peace﴾ means: it will be said to them, "Enter this Garden in safety from distress, grief, and fear."

(p-5514) ﴿That is the Day of Eternity.﴾ ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish﴾ [Qaf: 35] means: of what their souls desire and what delights their eyes. ﴿And with Us is more﴾ [Qaf: 35] means: of what does not occur to their minds, "that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard."

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[36] ﴿How many generations did We destroy before them, which were mightier than them in strength, so they roamed through the lands. Was there any escape?﴾

﴿How many did We destroy before them﴾, i.e., before these polytheists of Quraysh, ﴿generations which were mightier than them in strength﴾, i.e., in power, such as ʿAd, Pharaoh and Thamud, ﴿so they roamed through the lands﴾, i.e., they traveled through them, journeyed, and went around their farthest regions. Imru' al-Qays said:

"I have roamed the horizons until I was content with returning from the spoils."

﴿Was there any escape?﴾ i.e., did they, by their roaming through the lands, find any means of escape from the destruction they were promised because of their denial of the truth? According to this reading, the pronoun in "naqqabū" (they roamed) refers to the generations who were mightier in strength. It is also permissible for it to refer to these polytheists, meaning: they traveled on their journeys through the lands of the earlier generations; so did they find any escape for themselves, such that they might expect the like for themselves?

Ibn Jarir said: The reciters read His words ﴿fa-naqqabū﴾ with a doubled letter and a fatha on the qaf, in the form of a report about them. It is reported from Yahya ibn Yaʿmar that he used to read ﴿fa-naqqabū﴾ with a kasra on the qaf, in the form of a threat and warning, meaning: roam through the lands and wander in them, for you will not escape Us by means of yourselves.

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying:

[37] ﴿Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or gives ear while he is a witness.﴾

﴿Indeed, in that﴾, i.e., in the destruction of the generations that were destroyed before Quraysh, ﴿is a reminder﴾. ﴿For whoever has a heart﴾, i.e., it is a reminder by which whoever among this nation has understanding is reminded, so that he refrains from the deed they used to commit in their disbelief in their Lord, out of fear that there will befall them the like of what befell them of punishment.

﴿Or gives ear﴾, i.e., listens attentively with his hearing to the reports about these generations that were destroyed.

﴿While he is a witness﴾, i.e., present of heart, comprehending what is reported about them, not heedless or inattentive. It is also said that ﴿shahid﴾ is from the verb "shuhud," which means presence, and the intended meaning is one who is alert, because one who is not alert is like an absent person. Thus it is a metaphor (istiʿara) or a figurative usage (majaz mursal). Or ﴿shahid﴾ is in the sense of ﴿shahid﴾ (the one present), and there is an elided genitive (mudaf muqaddar) in it, meaning: present is his mind. Or it is from testimony (al-shahada), and the intended meaning is: a witness to its truth, i.e., one who affirms it, because he is the believer who benefits from it. This is a metonymy (kinaya) for the believer, as transmitted by al-Shihab.

A subtle point:

It has been said: the particle (أو) is for dividing the one who takes heed into one who recites and one who listens, or into a jurist and a learner, or into a scholar of complete readiness who needs nothing beyond reflecting on what he already has, and a deficient one who needs to learn, so he takes heed when he turns to it wholeheartedly and removes all the obstacles entirely. In the indefiniteness of (the heart) and its vagueness is glorification and an indication that every heart that does not reflect and does not ponder is as if it were no heart.

(p-5516)

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[38] ﴿And We certainly created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us.﴾

﴿And We certainly created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us.﴾ That is: weariness (ʾiʿyāʾ).

Qatadah said: "Allah refuted the Jews and the people of slander against Allah. That is because they said: Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, then He rested on the seventh day, and that day, according to them, is the Day of Saturday, and they call it the Day of Rest (yawm al-rāḥah)."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 50, verses 39–40:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[39–40] ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ ﴿And during part of the night glorify Him, and after the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 40]

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾ means: the polytheists' denial of the Resurrection, of Divine Oneness, and of prophethood. ﴿And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ ﴿And during part of the night glorify Him, and after the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 40], i.e., after the prayers (a'qab al-salawat). The intended meaning of "tasbih" (glorification) is either its apparent sense, which accompanies tahmid (praise), or it is prayer, by way of mentioning a part and intending the whole (itlaq al-juz'), or mentioning something necessarily associated with the whole (al-lazim 'ala al-kull), or mentioning what is necessitated by it (al-mazum). Accordingly, "before the rising" is the Dawn prayer (al-Subh). "Before the setting" is the Dhuhr and 'Asr prayers. "During part of the night" is the 'Isha' prayers and the tahajjud (night prayer). "And after the prostrations" refers to the supererogatory prayers (al-nawafil) after the obligatory prayers (al-maktubat).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 50, verses 41–42:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[41–42] ﴿And listen on the day the caller calls from a near place﴾ ﴿On the day they hear the Cry in truth; that is the Day of Emergence﴾ [Qaf: 42]

﴿And listen on the day the caller calls from a near place﴾ That is: listen, i.e., to what We have informed you of concerning the terrors of the Resurrection, on the day its caller calls from every near place, such that his call reaches all equally.

Al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) said: Perhaps it is, in the restoration, like "Be!" (kun) in the initial creation; that is, it is an illustration of the bringing of the dead to life by mere will, even if there is no call and no voice.

In the command coming in an unrestricted form, then its clarification by what follows it, there is an awe-inspiring magnification of the thing reported, because of what lies in obscurity followed by explanation of the awe and grandeur of the matter spoken of.

﴿On the day they hear the Cry﴾ [Qaf: 42] That is: the Cry of the Resurrection from the graves and the gathering for recompense, in truth. Ibn Jarir said: meaning, by the command to respond to Allah, to the place of reckoning.

﴿That is the Day of Emergence﴾ [Qaf: 42] That is: from the graves.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[43] ﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return.﴾

﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death﴾ — i.e., in this world, by bestowing the light of life or cutting it off. ﴿And to Us is the final return﴾ — i.e., the return of all of them on the Day of Resurrection.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[44] ﴿On the Day the earth splits asunder from them, rushing forth; that is a gathering, easy for Us.﴾

﴿On the Day the earth splits asunder from them, rushing forth⦆ means: they will come out of it hastening. ﴿That is a gathering, easy for Us⦆ means: that bringing-forth and assembling of them at the station of reckoning is easy for Us, without any burden.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[45] ﴿We know best what they say, and you are not over them a compeller. So remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My warning.﴾

﴿We know best what they say﴾ means: the polytheists of Makkah, concerning their slander against Allah and His Messenger, and their denial of His power over resurrection. This is a consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and a threat to them.

﴿And you are not over them a compeller﴾ means: not one who has authority and dominance to force them to faith. ﴿So remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My warning﴾ means: rather, you were only sent as a reminder and a conveyer (of the message). So remind, by what has been revealed to you, whoever fears the warning with which whoever disobeys and transgresses has been threatened, for he is the one who benefits from it.

Among the supplications of Qatadah: "O Allah, make us among those who fear Your warning and hope for Your promise, O Most Righteous, O Most Merciful."
